thesis: Knowledge increases specific responsibilities, while distributed technology must retain real avenues for correction.

ideas.statement: Research choices and honest uncertainty matter before downstream use, without requiring omnipotence or immediate utility.
Expertise does not determine human worth or confer universal competence.
Human oversight requires time, information and authority; unknown errors still create future duties once discovered.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A signature on an algorithmic recommendation can conceal powerless oversight.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Ethics review is not proven long-term harm reduction; dual-use restrictions also impose costs.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
